title: The fight, the room camera
why: The whole palette in one frame: near-black rock, one warm shaft, a lit pool, fire as the only saturated colour.

title: Fire and the lens at work
why: Effects read as thin bright lines on dark: the light is the drawing.

title: The shaft, cropped from the room camera
why: The same composition as the It Follows cover: a vertical beam onto a small pale egg; at game resolution the lich is a few pixels.

title: Burned mask (viewer)
why: Sooted porcelain, gashes, a pierced eye: the most face-like object, a ready emblem.

title: The hand (viewer)
why: The Sabazios blessing gesture: an icon of power given (and of giving it up).

title: Lodestone (viewer)
why: Raw, dark, weathered: the heaviest silhouette of the six.

title: Psyonian orbs (viewer)
why: Clear glass spheres: the only object that is several things.

title: Prismatic gem (viewer)
why: The one rainbow in a game of amber: the prismatic accent's source.

title: Attack lens (viewer)
why: A glass disc with one burning point of light: almost a logo already.

title: THE ENDING: the lich arched back beside the covered egg
why: The Kaen pose in the game, next to the egg wrapped in snakes; store art may not show the ending, so this is the source of a pose, not a frame to use.

title: THE ENDING: the two-shot in darkness
why: Everything but the two figures gone to black: the game's own most graphic image.

title: THE ENDING: the egg alone, lit from inside
why: One pale-gold egg on black: the simplest image the game makes.

title: The prismatic beam (round 18 sheet, older cave)
why: His bones' colours as a streaming rainbow: the beam is the game's prismatic accent in motion.
license: the game (round 18, before the cave surfaces changed)
